REV-1 [R9] R9 requires every app to open in the calm default - git tools collapsed, git drawer closed, console hidden. Creating and opening an app via 'Add app' -> save bypasses the calm reset that openApp applies, so a stale git drawer (and possibly expanded git tools) reappears in the new app. Route this new-app app-view transition through the same reset used by openApp (setGitTab(null), setGitToolsOpen(false), select the app's first terminal) instead of calling setView("app") directly.

REV-2 [USR-003] The suite is timing-sensitive/flaky under full parallel load; the build report claims a clean full run. Not certainly caused by this revision, but it should be stabilised before relying on the green result.
QA-1 [R8] Hiding the git drawer loses the in-progress commit message, so R8's edge case 'Hiding the git drawer does not ... lose an in-progress git message' is not met and is not covered by a test.

QA-2 [R7] R7's edge case that hide/show commands for every hideable tool (git tools, git drawer, console) appear in the palette and can hide/reopen the tool is proven only for the console; the git-tools and git-drawer palette commands have no test.

QA-3 [R9] R9's restart edge cases - a console open at close is not restarted and old output is not restored, and a dialog/banner/branch menu/theme finder/app edit form open at close is not reopened with stale content - have no test; only the sidebar flag is exercised across a restart.

QA-4 [R10] R10's plan-based acceptance - each building block's package or in-house decision, the jattac fallback, licence/maintenance/React 18.3 compatibility and reuse-before-adding - is not proven by any test; only the cmdk adoption and lazy load are.
QA-5 [R6] R6's edge case that the footer toggle and Ctrl+B agree when the editor is focused is not directly tested.
QA-6 [R7] The acceptance that the palette lists every app-level command in the plan's command list is only spot-checked, not asserted exhaustively.
QA-7 [R7] The acceptance clause that the editor's own file commands are not listed as palette commands is not asserted by any test.
QA-8 [R8] R8's edge cases 'hiding one tool leaves the rest of the layout as it was' and 'a hidden tool still surfaces its signal' are not directly asserted.
QA-9 [R7] The accessibility check's keyboard-only path (run a palette command with the keyboard, visible focus at each step, sensible focus after a tool closes) has no test.
